ei.title: A Brief History of Ellis Island
ei.subject: Ellis Island (양지원 학교 유인물)
ei.section: A Brief History of Ellis Island

fullPassage: In the late 1800s, people in many parts of the world decided to leave their homes for reasons such as crop failure, land and job shortages, rising taxes, famine, and relief from political and religious persecution. Perceiving the United States as the land of opportunity, nearly 12 million immigrants immigrated to the United States between 1870 and 1900. Together, these immigrants shaped a big part of the work force that drove the industrialization of America and helped the United States emerge as an industrial powerhouse. During this time, more than 70 percent of all immigrants entered through New York City, which came to be known as the “Golden Door.” Around 1892 when Ellis Island opened as a new immigration processing center, Americans became concerned with the “quality” of immigrants arriving in the country. The 1891 Immigration Act had set the course of American immigration policy for the next thirty years by expanding the types of “undesirable” immigrants. In addition to physical problems such as poor eyesight, bad backs, and trachoma, Ellis Island officials were on the lookout for “idiots, insane persons, paupers or persons likely to become public charges, persons suffering from a loathsome or a dangerous disease, persons who have been convicted of a crime or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude, polygamists.” In the coming decades, the list kept growing. In the 1920s, various immigration quota acts restricted immigration in numbers. The role Ellis Island held gradually shifted to that of a detention center for suspected Nazi and fascist sympathizers, and later, for suspected Communists and other radicals awaiting deportation. By 1954, an increasingly irrelevant Ellis Island closed its doors. Today, Ellis Island has transformed into a popular tourist attraction, after processing at least one ancestor of some 40 percent of Americans, according to estimations. As America deals with the challenges of our latest wave of mass immigration, it will do so without Ellis Island. But Ellis Island as myth, as a memory place, still has an important hold on the American imagination, and future generations will grapple with both its historical meaning and its relevance to contemporary, multicultural America.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ②emerging → emerge. help는 목적어 뒤에 원형부정사(또는 to부정사)를 쓰므로 helped ... emerge가 맞아요. -ing형은 올 수 없어요.
det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④relevant → relevance. 'both A and B' 구문에서 A(its historical meaning)가 명사이므로, and 뒤 B도 명사(relevance)로 맞춰야 해요. 형용사 relevant는 안 돼요.

④ relevant ❌ — 'grapple with both its historical meaning and its ___'는 'both A and B(A와 B 둘 다)' 구문이에요. A가 명사(meaning)이니 and 뒤도 명사여야 해서 relevance(관련성)가 맞고, 형용사 relevant는 짝이 안 맞아 틀려요 ←정답
det.tip: 'both A and B'는 A와 B의 품사·형태를 똑같이 맞춰요. 명사(meaning) and 명사(relevance).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정답: restricted immigration in numbers(이민을 수치상으로 제한했다). 빈칸 앞 quota acts(할당법)가 결정적 단서예요.

③ celebrated cultural diversity openly(문화적 다양성을 공개적으로 기렸다) ❌ — 본문에 근거가 없어요.

④ expanded job opportunities nationwide(전국의 일자리를 늘렸다) ❌ — 일자리 확대 이야기는 나오지 않아요.

밑줄 문장: 'As America deals with the challenges of our latest wave of mass immigration, it will do so without Ellis Island(미국이 최신 대규모 이민의 도전에 대응할 때, 그것은 엘리스 섬 없이 그렇게 할 것이다)'.

① 미래 세대 ❌ — 다음 문장에 나오는 별개의 소재예요.

② 엘리스 섬 ❌ — 바로 뒤 'without Ellis Island'에 나오는 함정이에요. it은 엘리스 섬 '없이' 행동하는 주체이지 엘리스 섬이 아니에요.

③ 미국 ✅ — 앞 절의 주어 America를 대신 받는 대명사예요 ←정답

④ 최신 대규모 이민의 물결 ❌ — 이민 물결은 미국이 '대응하는 대상'이지 행동의 주체가 아니에요.
det.tip: 대명사 it은 주로 앞 절의 주어를 받아요. 여기서는 As절의 주어 America(미국)예요. 바로 옆 Ellis Island에 속지 마세요.

엘리스 섬
미국
최신 대규모 이민의 물결

questions.passage: In the late 1800s, people in many parts of the world decided to leave their homes for reasons such as crop failure, land and job shortages, rising taxes, famine, and relief from political and religious persecution. Perceiving the United States as the land of opportunity, nearly 12 million immigrants immigrated to the United States between 1870 and 1900. Together, these immigrants shaped a big part of the work force that drove the industrialization of America and helped the United States emerge as an industrial powerhouse. During this time, more than 70 percent of all immigrants entered through New York City, which came to be known as the “Golden Door.” Around 1892 when Ellis Island opened as a new immigration processing center, Americans became concerned with the “quality” of immigrants arriving in the country. The 1891 Immigration Act had set the course of American immigration policy for the next thirty years by expanding the types of “undesirable” immigrants. In addition to physical problems such as poor eyesight, bad backs, and trachoma, Ellis Island officials were on the lookout for “idiots, insane persons, paupers or persons likely to become public charges, persons suffering from a loathsome or a dangerous disease, persons who have been convicted of a crime or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude, polygamists.” In the coming decades, the list kept growing. In the 1920s, various immigration quota acts restricted immigration in numbers. The role Ellis Island held gradually shifted to that of a detention center for suspected Nazi and fascist sympathizers, and later, for suspected Communists and other radicals awaiting deportation. By 1954, an increasingly irrelevant Ellis Island closed its doors. Today, Ellis Island has transformed into a popular tourist attraction, after processing at least one ancestor of some 40 percent of Americans, according to estimations. As America deals with __________, it will do so without Ellis Island. But Ellis Island as myth, as a memory place, still has an important hold on the American imagination, and future generations will grapple with both its historical meaning and its relevance to contemporary, multicultural America.

① the benefits of closing all national borders(모든 국경을 닫는 것의 이점) ❌ — 국경 폐쇄 이야기는 본문에 없어요.

② the challenges of our latest wave of mass immigration(최신 대규모 이민의 도전 과제) ✅ — 이 글의 주제(이민)와 이어지며, '엘리스 섬 없이 대응한다'는 뒷부분과도 맞아요 ←정답

③ the profits made from selling historic landmarks(역사 유적을 팔아 얻는 수익) ❌ — 유적 매각 이야기는 없어요.

④ the decline of interest in family genealogy(가계 연구에 대한 관심 감소) ❌ — 관심 감소를 다루지 않아요.
det.tip: 글 전체 주제가 '이민'이에요. 미국이 지금도 '새로운 대규모 이민의 과제'에 대응한다는 흐름이 자연스러워요.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]을 사용하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.
엘리스 섬은 새로운 이민 심사 센터로 문을 열었다.
[조건] (1) a, as, center, Ellis, immigration, Island, new, opened, processing을 모두 사용할 것
(2) 9단어로 쓸 것
(영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: '문을 열었다'가 핵심이라 주어 Ellis Island 뒤에 과거동사 opened를 놓고, '~로서'는 as로, 뒤에 명사구 a new immigration processing center를 이어요.
det.analysis:
우리말 '엘리스 섬은 새로운 이민 심사 센터로 문을 열었다'를 어순대로 옮겨요.

→ 주어 Ellis Island(엘리스 섬) + 과거동사 opened(문을 열었다).
→ '~로서/~로'는 전치사 as로 이어요.
→ 무엇으로? a new immigration processing center(새로운 이민 심사 센터). 형용사·명사 순서는 a → new → immigration → processing → center로 쌓아요.

따라서 'Ellis Island opened as a new immigration processing center'가 돼요.
det.tip: '~로 문을 열다'는 open as ~로 써요. 명사를 여러 개 쌓을 땐 a new immigration processing center 순서로 붙여요.

questions.passage: The 1891 Immigration Act had set the course of American immigration policy for the next thirty years by expanding the types of “undesirable” immigrants. In addition to physical problems such as poor eyesight, bad backs, and trachoma, Ellis Island officials were on the lookout for “idiots, insane persons, paupers or persons likely to become public charges, persons suffering from a loathsome or a dangerous disease, persons who have been convicted of a crime or misdemeanor __________ (involve) moral turpitude, polygamists.”
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 빈칸은 앞의 명사 a crime or misdemeanor(범죄나 경범죄)를 뒤에서 꾸미는 자리라, 현재분사 involving(~을 수반하는)으로 바꿔 써요.
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'persons who have been convicted of a crime or misdemeanor ___ (involve) moral turpitude'.

→ 빈칸 뒤에 목적어 moral turpitude(도덕적 타락)가 바로 나와요. 즉 빈칸은 앞의 명사(a crime or misdemeanor)를 꾸미면서 목적어를 취하는 자리예요.
→ 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미며 능동으로 목적어를 취하려면 현재분사(-ing)를 써요.
→ involve(수반하다) → involving(~을 수반하는).

따라서 정답은 involving이에요.
det.tip: 명사 뒤에서 꾸미며 뒤에 목적어(moral turpitude)를 데리고 오면 현재분사 -ing예요. involve → involving.

→ 무엇을 이끌었나? the industrialization of America(미국의 산업화). 'of America'는 industrialization 뒤에 붙여요.

따라서 'the work force that drove the industrialization of America'가 돼요.
det.tip: '~한 노동력'처럼 명사를 문장으로 꾸밀 땐 관계대명사 that을 써요. 'A의 B'는 the B of A 순서예요.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [보기]의 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.
모든 이민자의 70퍼센트 이상이 뉴욕시를 통해 들어왔다
[보기] 70, all, City, entered, immigrants, more, New, of, percent, than, through, York
(12단어, 영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: '~퍼센트 이상'은 more than 70 percent, '모든 이민자의'는 of all immigrants, '들어왔다'는 entered, '~를 통해'는 through로 이어요.
det.analysis:

→ 주어부: more than 70 percent(70퍼센트 이상) + of all immigrants(모든 이민자의).
→ 동사: entered(들어왔다).
→ 어디를 통해? through New York City(뉴욕시를 통해). 장소 이름 New York City는 그대로 이어 붙여요.

따라서 'more than 70 percent of all immigrants entered through New York City'가 돼요.
det.tip: '~ 이상'은 more than, '~를 통해'는 through예요. 'A의 B퍼센트'는 B percent of A 순서로 놓아요.
